questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I thought about choosing a country that had a unique nature to explore. Canada is large country that has a lot of variation in terms of landscape and animals, and I thought it would be cool to see how it was to live in a country that had all that. Other than that, I thought it would be nice to get the experience of going to an American university as each university has its own sports facility, and it was something I wanted to see.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I think I was a really good idea to go on exchange. I got to know people from all around the world and I got to experience things I would never be able to in Denmark. This included going to ice hockey- and basketball matches as well as meeting new people from different countries. I was satisfied with what I got to explore but there were some elements in living in Hamilton which I didn't really like and was tired of which for example was trash lying around where I lived and just not the cleanest environment. Another thing is that I didn't get to see my family and friends as much as I am used to, so some of the weekends were maybe not as fun as in my home country. When that is said, I still think it's good to see how it is living aboard and I think I got to appreciate the things I didn't have there more.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I don't think it was that difficult to find the information needed. The university had a welcome week before the first classes, and I got an orientation around campus and attended some events. There were some booths where I could ask questions if I had any, so once I started university, I think I had the information that was necessary to study there.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As explained in the previous question, the university held a welcome week where I could ask the questions I had. The university sent me some emails too about what was coming up, but I wasn't like I was in need for any help when I arrived other than that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was satisfied; I think the university did a good job with the welcome week. One thing I remember which I didn't like was that everybody was offered a buddy before we came, who could answer some of the questions we had and set us up with other exchange students, my buddy didn't answer the questions I asked. I ended up joining a group that had an active buddy so it didn't really have an effect but still a bit annoying and I think it could cause some trouble for some students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I rented a room through Airbnb which was an easy process. I had a good host, and everything worked as it should. In the beginning of the year, I tried to get a residence spot on campus but unfortunately there weren't enough rooms for that. I then tried to find off campus housing with the link the university had sent me but the landlord's happened to have some discrimination in terms of their gender policy since most would only allow girls to live there. Overall, I think I spent a lot of time with the links the university provided me which didn't benefit me at all. It was much easier to find a place though Airbnb even though it was a bit expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They should know that it can take some time to get to campus, especially when the buses strike.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Just as expressed in the first question about housing. I spent a lot of time with the links the university had provided, but in the end my time was wasted, and I could just have gone directly to Airbnb and be sure to have a place to live instead of the long process I had which didn't pay off.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As I remember I spent some days on different weeks trying to register the courses. I didn't know how to do it the first times I tried but after giving it a break and multiple tries I finally did it. Looking back at it I don't think it was that difficult, but sometimes you have a bad day.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When the university had sent me my log in details, I could go to their website and press on the box called "Create MyTimetable" I could select the courses I wanted by typing the name of the course in a search box. When selecting a course, a schedule showed up for when the classes were and after choosing the courses I wanted, I could press on a button called "get this schedule".

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I actually don't remember; I think I did it all on my own.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful, I got the exact classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would say a good idea is to register early as all the classes are available at that time. I saw that it wasn't possible to register some of the courses I had chosen in end of the period.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think I got what I expected. I think two out of my four teachers were very good, and the things that were thought were similar to what I have learned at University of Copenhagen, though it was a bit easier than what I previous had had.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was third year courses and as mentioned before, I think it was easier than at Copenhagen. I think the things that were thought, were important and it was nice to get some knowledge on the courses I hadn't had in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I would say the style of teaching was the same as in Copenhagen. I think there was a tendency for the teacher to go over the things that were thought in the last lecture a bit more than what the teachers do in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON 3SO3: Industrial Organization
ECON 3EO3: Applied Econometrics
ECON 3DO3: Labour Economics
ECON 3HH3: International Trade

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend taking Labour Economics and International Trade. I would say I had a good lecturer in Applied Econometrics too.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think I encountered any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The tickets to watch a hockey match in the weekends were expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was satisfied with the sports facilities the university had. The only thing I didn't like was that there were a lot of people in the gym doing the weekdays which meant that I most likely would have to wait to do the exercises I wanted to.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Badminton, basketball, cricket, dodgeball, flag football, floorball, ice hockey, pickleball, soccer, softball, spikeball, table tennis, touch rugby, ultimate frisbee and volleyball.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend trying badminton. It is a nice activity, and it was nice to try the intramural.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend going to Toronto to watch an ice hockey or basketball match in Scotia Bank Arena and just explore the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I don't think it was hard to adjust to the local culture. The thing that annoyed me was that there is not as clean of an environment in Canada as there is at home. Other than that, I think I had an easy time adjusting to the local culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: In Canada people are very open minded and it is not difficult to speak to them. Plenty of students actually approached me, so there are many of them that want to talk. Having this in mind, I had an easier time speaking to other students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't think there were any to be honest.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I think going to different places and see what the nature looked like was a thing I appreciated as well as observing how they held events on stadiums. I thought it was good to experience the things Americans do and to see what they have in general.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Having a good beginning is the most important thing. Get to know as many people as possible from the start so you have a bunch of people you are connected to. It is better to have people writing to you and you declining the invitation, rather than having nobody writing to you or you having nobody around to write to, when you want to go out.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The other important thing would be attending the welcome week. It is a good place to meet other exchange students and a nice beginning. Remember that other exchange students are in the same boat as you, and they would like to get some new friends too.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I think the most rewarding thing was getting to know I had an easy time living in a foreign country without the people I am used to having around. One thing is to be sure you can do it, but another thing is actually doing it. I think I had satisfied feeling after my exchange ended.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think the greatest challenge was the thing that made it the most rewarding experience, exactly not having my friends and family around. It was most challenging in the weekends as I would usually see either of them in my home country.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy your time on exchange, it is not an opportunity everybody gets!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
